=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: AI spec orchestration platform that converts plain-English briefs into structured user story specs and autonomously executes them story-by-story via isolated agent subprocesses (claude, opencode, or codex)

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript 5.7 (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom 7
  - framer-motion
  - recharts
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - pg-boss (job queue)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - tsx (TypeScript runner)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary UI panels (Specs, Runs, Analytics, Direction, Settings)
  - src/components/ — shared UI (Sidebar, RunTerminal, CommandPalette, slide-overs)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files
  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)
  - backend/src/worker.ts — pg-boss worker process (pipeline job consumer)
  - backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts — sole execution engine for all agent types
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL pool, migration runner, 70+ migrations
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (24 tools)
  - forge/ — spec JSON files, run-loop.sh bash fallback, self-register script

constraints:
  - Migrations must use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files (sequential 001-079 already exist)
  - Worker process must be running for pipeline triggers to execute
  - AGE search_path must be restored after every graph query
  - Auth middleware is globally disabled (intentional, local tool)
  - CLAUDE_BIN full path required for child process spawning (NVM PATH not inherited)
  - spec id is always the filename slug, never the human title

deployment_target: local (self-hosted, npm run dev) or Docker Compose

ports:
  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

integrations:
  - claude CLI (claude --print)
  - opencode CLI (opencode run)
  - codex CLI (codex --approval-mode auto-edit)
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks
  - Linear (post-launch)
  - Vercel (post-launch)
  - Slack (post-launch)
  - Stripe billing

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Fix context injection gaps so OpenCode and Codex agents receive the SAME effective context as Claude during Rorca pipeline story execution. Currently buildPrompt() in execution-engine.ts constructs an identical prompt for all agents, but Claude's binary auto-discovers additional context that OpenCode/Codex miss:

GAP 1 — CLAUDE.md not explicitly injected: Claude binary auto-reads workspace root CLAUDE.md (~5-18K tokens of architecture context). buildPrompt() does NOT inject it — it relies on Claude's native auto-discovery. OpenCode and Codex binaries don't read CLAUDE.md. FIX: Add CLAUDE.md content as a global context source in the CIE-004 context router (priority 101, always included). This means adding it to .rorca/config.json globals automatically during workspace setup, or injecting it directly in buildPrompt() for non-claude agents. The content should be injected into contextPreamble so all agents see it.

GAP 2 — .claude/skills/ not mirrored: Claude binary auto-loads all .claude/skills/*.md files natively. buildPrompt() explicitly SKIPS .claude/skills/ for Claude (to avoid double-injection) and only loads .rorca/skills/ for matched skills. If a skill exists in .claude/skills/ but NOT in .rorca/skills/, OpenCode/Codex miss it entirely. FIX: During pipeline trigger (or during skill install), ensure every skill in .claude/skills/ has a mirror in .rorca/skills/. Add a sync function that copies any .claude/skills/*.md that don't have .rorca/skills/ equivalents. Run this sync before each pipeline run for non-claude agents.

GAP 3 — Workflow skill contains Claude-specific syntax: .claude/skills/rorca.md (or dimitri.md) is the workflow skill injected by buildPrompt() for all agents. It may contain Claude Code-specific instructions like Task(subagent_type="Explore") or references to Claude-only tools. OpenCode/Codex will ignore or misinterpret these. FIX: Make buildPrompt() strip or replace Claude-specific tool references when agent is not claude. Create an agentNormalizeSkill(content, agentType) function that: for opencode — replaces Task() subagent calls with "use grep/glob/read to explore"; for codex — similar replacements. Apply this to skillContent (workflow skill) and matchedSkills before injection.

GAP 4 — Context audit endpoint: There is no way to compare what each agent type would receive. FIX: Add GET /api/pipeline/context-audit?workspaceId=X&specId=Y&storyId=Z&agent=claude|opencode|codex that returns the full buildPrompt() output for a given story under each agent type. This lets users verify parity before running. Include token counts per section (direction, memory, skills, graph, CLAUDE.md, workflow skill, persona, story task).

GAP 5 — Integration test: Add a test that runs buildPrompt() for the same story under all 3 agent types and asserts the effective context (minus agent-specific boilerplate like "read SKILL.md") has the same semantic content. This prevents future regressions where a new context source is added for one agent but not others.

IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS:
- Do NOT change what Claude receives (it works perfectly)
- Only ADD context for OpenCode/Codex to match Claude's effective context
- The context-router (CIE-004) already has globals, scoped, tagged, and memory sections — use this infrastructure
- buildPrompt() in execution-engine.ts is the single point of truth for prompt assembly
- pipeline.ts already has writeOpenCodeSkillFile() and writeCodexAgentsMd() for pre-run direction stack injection
- Skills are matched via LLM in skill-matcher.ts and loaded via loadMatchedSkills() in execution-engine.ts
- Memory is injected via memory-ledger.ts getContextSnippet() through context-router writeContextFile()
- The direction stack (L1-L5) is already injected identically for all agents (via different delivery mechanisms but same content)
